ORGANIZATION_SUBTITLE: Meet the team behind the vision of a modern Serbia. The Serbian Democratic League gathers experts, visionaries, and dedicated individuals who believe in democratic values and institutional stability.
PRESIDENT_BIO: As the founder and president of SDL, Prof. Dr. Jovanović has been contributing to the political scene of Serbia for two decades through academic work and public advocacy for transparency and the rule of law. His vision is Serbia as a leader in regional integration and an economically stable state.
JOIN_TEAM_SUBTITLE: We believe in the power of unity and professionalism. Become a part of the movement that changes Serbia for the better.
SDL_HERO_SUBTITLE: The first political party of Serbs in the Ottoman Empire, founded in Skopje in 1908.
SDL_CONTEXT_P1: After the Young Turk Revolution in July 1908, Serbs in the Ottoman Empire recognized a moment to change their approach. Armed struggle was suspended and the focus moved to political organization.
SDL_CONTEXT_P2: The Serbian Democratic League was founded at the First Serbian Conference held in Skopje from August 10 to 13, 1908. The goal was to organize the Serbian people into one whole and support the establishment of constitutional life in the Empire.
SDL_CALLOUT_TEXT_PREFIX: Sessions were held in the new premises of the Serbian Club in the building of
SDL_CALLOUT_TEXT_SUFFIX: , where both the club and the editorial office of the "Vardar" newspaper were located.
SDL_IMAGE_VARDAR_ALT: Building of the Vardar newspaper editorial office
SDL_IMAGE_VARDAR_CAPTION: Building of the "Vardar" newspaper editorial office in Skopje.
SDL_MANIFEST_QUOTE: "Turn beautiful words into real material foundations of our state life."
SDL_PRINCIPLE_1: Abandoning revolutionary organization and moving to legal constitutional struggle.
SDL_PRINCIPLE_2: Absolute preservation of the integrity of the Ottoman Empire as the basis of work.
SDL_PRINCIPLE_3: Agreement with all other elements in the Empire to establish and stabilize constitutional life.
SDL_COMMITTEE_SUBTITLE: Leaders of the Serbian people elected at the First Conference in Skopje.
SDL_IMAGE_COMMITTEE_CAPTION: Interim central committee of the Organization of Ottoman Serbs, July 1908.
SDL_ASSEMBLY_TITLE: First Assembly of Serbs in the Ottoman Empire (1909)
SDL_ASSEMBLY_SUBTITLE: Held in Skopje from February 2 to 11, 1909.
SDL_RESOLUTION_1_TEXT: Strict respect for law, freedoms and equal rights was demanded, along with free use of the Serbian name and condemnation of the annexation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
SDL_RESOLUTION_2_TEXT: Privileges were requested for Serbian metropolitans, as well as rights for Serbs in dioceses without a Serbian metropolitan, including free choice between a Serbian or Bulgarian priest.
SDL_RESOLUTION_3_TEXT: The return of seized property and enabling peasants to buy land were demanded, with emphasis on modernization of crafts and trade through their own banking institutions.
SDL_GALLERY_1_CAPTION: An issue of the "Vardar" newspaper with the League program.
SDL_GALLERY_2_CAPTION: Interior of the hall where the 1909 Assembly was held.
SDL_GALLERY_3_CAPTION: Correspondence and seals of the Central Committee.
